findings.problem: Two list-narrowing mechanisms with different semantics landed in one epic. E22-S04 added identity.service.granted_scopes (modules/identity/service.py:705), which expands a project grant down roll_down edges of authorization_scope and is called from routers (api/requisitions.py:148, api/sourcing.py:160, 609); a caller with no grant gets an empty 200 page. E22-S06 added kernel require_granted + IdentityResolver.granted_scopes (modules/identity/resolver.py:171), which returns direct assignments only, and a caller with no grant gets 403. Consequence: a user holding project.read and requisition.view on project P with a roll-down child C sees C's requisitions in the requisition list and may GET /projects/C (the check walks roll-down), but C is missing from GET /projects (projects/service.py:995 filters p.id = ANY(project_ids) of direct grants only; the ponytail note at :935 admits it). Same permission model, two answers, depending on which story wrote the list.
findings.fix: Keep one: make IdentityResolver.granted_scopes run the roll-down CTE from identity.service.granted_scopes and return GrantedScopes, move requisitions and RFQ lists onto require_granted, delete the service-level function, and pick one no-grant answer (403 per require_granted) for all three lists.

findings.problem: ProjectService.lookup_people is a byte-for-byte copy of RequisitionLookups._users (modules/requisitions/lookups.py:111): same SQL against identity/user_role, same escaping, same label/note shaping, same 'for naming sponsors' docstring. E22-S07 then had to add display_name to both. A third people search (approvals/delegation.py:244) differs only in its id filter.
findings.fix: Add one people_search(connection, scope, q, limit) to identity.service beside names_by_id/emails_by_id and call it from both lookups.

findings.problem: If-Match parsing (convention O) is copied inline again: set_display_name (E22-S07) repeats vendors.schemas.expected_version (E22-S04) word for word, including both error texts and if_match_required. The same block now exists in 12 modules (grep 'If-Match must contain an integer'). Each copy is a place the 400/409 shape can drift.
findings.fix: Move expected_version and the stale_version conflict into kernel (e.g. kernel/errors.py or a kernel/concurrency.py) and replace the copies; a follow-up chore, not this epic's blocker.

findings.problem: E22-S03's 'one audit helper' is not held by any gate: direct AuditWriter(...).write calls remain at vendors/service.py:417, projects/schedule.py:238, org/bootstrap.py:116, identity/explain.py:359, and per-module _audit wrappers remain in vendors (5 files), purchasing, collaboration, requisitions/amendments.py:88. New stories will keep adding wrappers because nothing fails when they do.
findings.fix: Either convert the remaining callers to kernel.audit.audit_event, or add a boundaries check that forbids AuditWriter outside kernel/audit with a planted-violation test.
